WHY THIS LIST

How value spreads

A company starts with a few builders. What they build reaches much further: to the customers who buy it, the people who make it and the savers who own it. Here is the case in four figures.

  1. 01 Value created

    Combined value of the companies, year-end 2024

    That value exists because customers chose what these companies make. Market value is a snapshot of equity, and it moves with share prices.

  2. 02 Livelihoods

    People employed directly, worldwide

    Together these companies pay those people an estimated a year. That is our estimate: people employed multiplied by an assumed yearly pay.

  3. 03 Shared ownership

    Of Amazon held outside its founder’s direct stake

    Jeff Bezos’s direct stake was , worth at year-end 2024. The other belonged to index funds, pension systems such as CalPERS, other institutions and individuals. Through funds and pensions, part of Amazon sits in people’s retirement savings.

    See who holds Amazon’s shares

  4. 04 Reach

    Amazon’s net sales in 2024

    Amazon reports those sales by market: . It also reports jobs, investment and estimated GDP contributions for U.S. states.

METHODOLOGY

How to read this list

Every figure is a fixed 2024–25 snapshot. Each profile links its sources.

Value created

Each company’s market capitalization at year-end 2024, from CompaniesMarketCap, as a snapshot of its equity value. It reflects the share price and the number of shares outstanding. Many people helped build that value; each profile highlights one leader connected to the company.

Discussion that inspired the list

People employed

People working directly for the company or its subsidiaries on the reporting date, including those who joined through acquisitions. Figures come from annual reports and Stock Analysis, generally for fiscal 2024 or the first half of 2025. Where reporting overlaps, some people may appear in more than one company’s total. Each profile links its source.

Estimated annual pay to workers

An estimate of the total yearly pay that supports workers’ livelihoods: people employed multiplied by an assumed yearly pay per person in USD. The assumption reflects the industry and, in some cases, the company’s home country. Actual pay varies by role and location. The slider on each profile shows how the estimate changes with the assumption.

Operating locations

Company globes show selected locations. Amazon’s map adds net sales by market, estimated GDP contributions and investment by U.S. state, and reported measures for selected facilities. Employment and pay figures at the top of each profile cover people worldwide. Globe geography comes from Natural Earth; U.S. state boundaries come from the Census Bureau through US Atlas. Photo credits and licenses appear on each profile.
